title: DOM Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Heatmap Tooltip via Unescaped Bucket Label
analysis:
A DOM-based Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) vulnerability exists in the Prometheus Web UI heatmap visualization component (`jquery.flot.heatmap.js`). **Data Flow:** 1. **Source**: Untrusted user input can enter either via URL parameters on the Prometheus Graph page (such as `g0.expr` containing a PromQL expression that sets or replaces the `le` label, e.g. via `label_replace()`, combined with `g0.display_mode=heatmap`) or via metric labels ingested from monitored scrape targets or remote write requests. 2. **Validation/Sanitization**: While other parts of the graph UI (such as `GraphHelpers.ts`) sanitize label values using `escapeHTML()`, `jquery.flot.heatmap.js` extracts `s?.labels?.le` and interpolates it directly into template literals (`labelHtml = '
Bucket: ' + (label || 'value') + '
'`) with zero escaping or sanitization. 3. **Sink**: `tooltip.innerHTML = '
' + timeHtml + '
' + labelHtml + valueHtml + '
'` followed by `document.body.appendChild(tooltip)` on mouse hover over a heatmap cell. **Conceptual Exploit Payload:** An attacker crafts a link to the Prometheus Web UI with a query that generates a series with an XSS payload in the `le` label and automatically enables heatmap view: ``` http://:9090/graph?g0.expr=label_replace(vector(1)%2C+%22le%22%2C+%22%3Cimg+src%3Dx+onerror%3Dalert(document.domain)%3E%22%2C+%22%22%2C+%22%22)&g0.tab=0&g0.display_mode=heatmap ``` When a user visits the link and hovers their cursor over the rendered heatmap chart, `mouseMoveHandler` triggers `showTooltip`, which assigns the unescaped `le` label containing the `` payload to `tooltip.innerHTML` and appends it to `document.body`, executing arbitrary JavaScript in the victim's browser context. Alternatively, an attacker controlling a monitored target can expose a histogram metric with a malicious `le` label value to achieve persistent stored XSS when users view heatmaps of that metric.
